assessment.nobel_worthiness: The political-economy framework for trade policy (the 'protection for sale' approach) turned lobbying and trade protection into tractable, testable models. It has shaped theory, empirical work and trade-policy analysis for three decades. The same pair's work on trade and endogenous growth adds to the case, though it falls outside this entry's stated discovery.
assessment.attribution: Two names with a long, tightly linked joint program. Credit is clean and there is little dispute over priority. Other contributors to the political-economy-of-protection literature exist but are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date from the 1990s and have had decades of confirmation, extension and use. Timing is not a concern.
uncertainties: Direct empirical support for the specific functional forms of the protection-for-sale model is mixed.
Helpman also appears in another trade entry, so committee choices among trade candidates could interact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Founded the modern intertemporal, microfounded approach to open-economy macroeconomics (the 'Redux' framework and the textbook synthesis). It also framed the exchange-rate disconnect and related puzzles that still organise the field and inform policy on exchange rates and capital flows.
assessment.attribution: Two names with a clear joint contribution. Rogoff's separate exchange-rate and crisis work is a further strength, but the entry should be judged on the joint framework. Credit to other open-economy macro pioneers is a minor risk.
assessment.maturity: Mid-1990s onward, with a long period of absorption into central-bank and academic practice. It is mature.
uncertainties: Some of the puzzles named in the entry are still unresolved, which makes the discovery framing partly a research agenda rather than a settled result.
Rogoff also appears in the financial-crises entry, so the committee may weigh which framing to reward.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 'Credit Cycles' model showed how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. It is a foundational mechanism in modern macro-finance and was heavily used after 2008. Its importance for understanding financial-friction-driven downturns is high.
assessment.attribution: A single seminal paper by two authors, and the credit is clear. Gertler and Gilchrist are credited for the financial-accelerator strand. That strand overlaps with the earlier Bernanke-Gertler work, with Bernanke already a laureate, so a Kiyotaki-Moore award is the cleaner attribution.
assessment.maturity: From 1997, with decades of subsequent work and a clear post-crisis revival. It is mature.
uncertainties: The committee may see the 2022 prize on banking and financial crises as having partly covered this ground.
Quantitative importance relative to other financial-friction mechanisms is debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, the New Keynesian synthesis and the rules-based theory of monetary policy underpin how central banks think and operate. Its practical and intellectual influence is very large.
assessment.attribution: This is the hardest entry to attribute. Eight names are credited, the cap is three, and Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and others made major contributions. Calvo (staggered pricing), Taylor (staggered contracts and the Taylor rule) and Woodford (the synthesis) are a defensible, but arguable, core.
assessment.maturity: The foundations date from the late 1970s and 1980s, with synthesis in the late 1990s and 2000s. It is fully mature.
uncertainties: Any three-person selection from this literature leaves out comparably important contributors.
Post-2008 and post-2021 inflation debates have questioned parts of the framework.
Prior macro prizes (Lucas, Sargent-Sims, Kydland-Prescott, Bernanke) partly overlap the territory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The trade-shock and task-based analyses of labour demand reshaped understanding of how globalisation and technology affect wages, employment and regional economies. Their policy and public influence is very large and clearly relevant to society.
assessment.attribution: The China-shock work is mainly Autor, Dorn and Hanson. The task-based framework also relies on contributions (including Katz and others) not all captured here. The 2024 prize and other recent prizes touch on technology and inequality, and attribution between the trade and tasks strands needs care.
assessment.maturity: Key papers date from about 2003 to 2016, with a decade of replication and debate. It is reasonably mature, but later than most other entries.
uncertainties: Debate continues over the long-run magnitude and interpretation of the China-shock effects.
The entry blends two literatures (trade shocks and tasks), which complicates the statement of a single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers bargaining model gave non-cooperative game theory a tractable, widely used account of bargaining. The extension to decentralised markets links it to search and matching theory. It is foundational theory with a wide downstream reach in labour, industrial organisation and macro.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is contested. Rubinstein's 1982 model is the anchor. Ståhl's independent finite-horizon contribution is not credited here. The Binmore-Rubinstein-Wolinsky work on the relationship to the Nash solution and on markets supports adding Binmore and Wolinsky.
assessment.maturity: From the early 1980s onward, so it is highly mature. The case rests on a theoretical foundation rather than recent empirical confirmation.
uncertainties: Others (including Ståhl) have a priority claim, which complicates a three-name selection.
Game-theory prizes already recognise nearby ground, so the committee may see partial overlap.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Built long-run top-income and wealth series from tax data and brought distributional measurement to the centre of economics. The influence on research and public debate is very large, and the data work is a durable public good.
assessment.attribution: The top-income series work is joint, with Piketty and Saez the original core. Zucman's offshore-wealth and distributional-accounts work is more recent. Credit for the series and for later conceptual claims should be kept separate, and Atkinson (deceased) had a precursor role.
assessment.maturity: The income-series work dates from about 2003, but the wealth and offshore strands are much more recent. Overall it is moderately mature.
uncertainties: Measurement choices (such as treatment of taxes, transfers and capital income) are contested and affect the level and trend of reported inequality.
The theoretical claims about the long-run capital-income dynamics are separate from the measurement contribution and are more debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design give a general framework for how a sender can optimally shape what others learn. It unifies and extends earlier information-economics results and is used in theory, platform design, regulation and applied work.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow wrote the canonical persuasion paper. Bergemann and Morris developed the broader information-design programme, so a three-name selection leaves out one core contributor either way.
assessment.maturity: From 2011 onward, so it is the youngest of the eight. The framework has been rapidly adopted, but the empirical and practical track record is shorter.
uncertainties: It is early for a prize, and the committee may prefer to wait for further consolidation.
Which of the four credited contributors would be selected is uncertain.
Real-world applications are growing but are not yet as well established as those of other candidates.
